digest.component_or_area: Cloud rate-limit sweep — jira adapter transport coverage
propositions: The Cloud rate-limit sweep's file list is hardcoded in _step0_names() rather than derived, so renamed or moved classified mutating methods escape the sweep without notice.

A classified mutating name can be moved from the four swept transport modules into unswept sibling modules (backend.py, acli_subprocess.py, jira_fields.py, etc.) without triggering a completeness assertion.

Option A (glob-derive all adapters/jira/*.py modules) widens the sweep's scope from transport layer to entire package and requires individual 429-policy classification of 90 members; Option B (explicit list with anti-drift guard) preserves transport scoping and guards only pure same-name self.transport delegations outside the sweep.

The operator decision (2026-08-07) mandates Option B: retain the explicit transport file list and add an AST-based anti-drift guard that accepts only pure delegating facades (single return statement forwarding arguments unchanged to self.transport.<same_name>).
Exactly two classified mutating names currently exist outside the swept modules—backend.py::set_relationship and backend.py::add_comment—both are benign pure delegations that pass the facade guard.

The guard must scan all unswept adapters/jira/*.py modules (including acli_subprocess.py and jira_fields.py) and reject any classified mutating name unless it is a provably pure same-name transport delegation.
